title: Endpoint Interop & Stability PRD + Preflight Launch Checklist
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines a tightly scoped effort to ensure behavioral compatibility, performance stability, and safe rollout for the hosted inference endpoints that power chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank. The goal is not to redesign the API surface, but to formalize interop guarantees, acceptance criteria, preflight tests, and an operational prelaunch checklist so product teams can depend on consistent semantics and SLOs across lanes and model variants.

Why now:
- Recent regressions in tokenization edge cases and KV-cache warmup increased variance in tail-latency for chat endpoints.
- Early customers reported embedding quality drift between model variants during fallback.
- Ambiguity about behavioral contracts for rerank endpoints caused integration rework for two enterprise customers.

Scope (in scope):
- Define endpoint behavioral contract for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank (input/response invariants, deterministic seeds where applicable, streaming semantics, error envelope).
- Automated interop suite that runs determinism and semantic regression checks across canonical prompt set and model variants.
- Performance stability targets: median latency target and 99th percentile SLOs for baseline traffic profiles.
- Preflight runbook and checklist for staged canary rollout and cutover.
- Observability dashboard templates and alert thresholds for acceptance metrics.

Out of scope:
- Major API surface changes (new protocols, new endpoints).
- Model architecture-level optimizations beyond existing runtime knobs.

Requirements and constraints:
- Behavior contract must be expressible as a set of automated checks (determinism tolerance, tokenization equivalence, structured output schema validation).
- Acceptance tests must run reproducibly in CI and on production-like traffic replay.
- Canary rollouts must support progressive traffic ramp and automated rollback on metric regressions.
- Changes must be compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments; where not possible, document differences.

Behavioral contracts (high level):
1) Chat: preserve message-level turn semantics and streaming boundaries. New minor model variants must not change the default assistant persona or stop token behavior for canonical prompts.
2) Completions: guarantees about prefix preservation when using prompt injection patterns; streaming flush and partial-completion markers must be stable.
3) Embeddings: cosine-distance adjacency relationships must be stable for production anchors within a tolerance band (explained in acceptance criteria).
4) Rerank: relative ordering of a canonical candidate set must not deviate beyond an agreed drift score without a flagged behavioral change and customer notice.

Acceptance criteria (must all be satisfied before final rollout):
- Functional: 
  - AC-1: Interop suite passes across 3 representative model variants (small, medium, large) for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank within a single CI run.
  - AC-2: Structured output schema validation passes for 100 canonical probe prompts for chat/completions with 0 schema failures.
  - AC-3: Streaming contract tests (start-of-stream, partial chunk markers, end-of-stream) pass for both chunked and non-chunked clients.
- Quality: 
  - AC-4: Embedding anchors maintain cosine similarity within +/- 0.02 on average and none exceed 0.05 drift against baseline vectors on the canonical set.
  - AC-5: Rerank relative ordering correlation (Spearman rho) >= 0.92 vs baseline for canonical candidate permutations.
- Performance / Reliability: 
  - AC-6: Median latency for standard generation request profile (512 prompt tokens, 64 generation tokens) <= 120ms for hosted-lane baseline.
  - AC-7: 99th percentile latency <= 800ms under synthetic QA traffic (QPS=200, burst policy applied).
  - AC-8: Error rate (5xx) < 0.2% sustained for 24h during ramp.
- Operational: 
  - AC-9: Canary automation correctly rolls back when alert thresholds are hit on staging > production mirror.
  - AC-10: Observability dashboard shows token-level cost, latency histogram, and per-route failure breakdown and is accessible by SRE and PM.

Preflight launch checklist (must be completed and signed off):
1) Documentation & Contracts: 
   - Publish the behavior contract doc and link it in the public API reference and internal playbook.
   - Notify affected customers (tenant list) with a summary of behavior guarantees and planned canary dates.
2) Automated tests: 
   - Interop suite green for 3 model variants in CI and nightly regression runs scheduled.
   - Streaming contract and schema tests added to pre-deploy gate.
3) Performance & Load: 
   - Load test run with production-like traffic profile, results saved to perf-dashboard and attached to ticket.
   - KV-cache warmup scenarios tested (cold, warm, repeated prefix).
4) Observability & Alerts: 
   - Dashboard templates deployed to Console for this release.
   - Alerts configured: latency-P0, error-rate-P0, rerank-drift-warning (P1), embeddings-drift-warning (P1).
5) Deployment & Canary: 
   - Canary pipeline prepared: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated checks at each stage.
   - Rollback playbook written and staged in runbooks with contact on-call rotation.
6) Security & Compliance: 
   - Confirm PKI/KMS integration not affected and logs/audit retained per compliance plan.
7) Release comms: 
   - Release notes drafted with breaking-change matrix (none expected).
   - Internal training session scheduled for Solutions and Support.

Rollout plan (summary):
- Day 0: Deploy to canary subset (5% traffic) for 6 hours; run non-regression, perf, and interop suite.
- Day 1: If canary metrics OK, ramp 5%->25% over 2 hours; monitor 48h for tail-latency and failure rate.
- Day 3: Ramp to 100% if no regressions and post-ramp regression suite passes.

Monitoring & runbooks:
- Post-deploy smoke checks run at 1m, 5m, 30m, 2h.
- On-call SRE runbook for endpoints includes immediate rollback criteria: 3x baseline 99th percentile latency sustained for 15m OR error rate spike > 0.5% sustained for 10m.

Tradeoffs and open decisions (work items):
- T1: Tightening embedding drift tolerance may increase false positives in alerting; agreed to start conservative and tighten over 2 cycles.
- T2: Some Dedicated customers require different rollback semantics; document divergence and gating.
- T3: Whether to treat minor persona shifts as acceptable model churn or require explicit customer opt-in; PM to finalize by 2025-03-05.

Artifacts & links:
- Canonical probe set (drive): https://drive.redwood/example/probeset (placeholder)
- Interop CI job: https://ci.redwood/integration/interop-suites
- Perf dashboard: https://console.redwood/perf/PM-531842
- Acceptance report template: https://docs.redwood/acceptance/templates/interop-acceptance

Business impact:
- Reduces integration churn for enterprise customers by minimizing contract surprises.
- Lowers runway for post-launch incidents and support escalations.

Next steps (immediate):
- PM to confirm probe set and finalize tolerances (owner: Marisol).
- ENG to wire the interop suite into CI and expose pass/fail artifact (owner: Liam O'Connor).
- SRE to create dashboard and hook alerts (owner: Kavita Rao).
